actions.body: Collective decision-making often faces the challenge of reconciling divergent individual viewpoints. Drawing on Wimsatt and Campbell’s robustness analysis, we explore how identifying cross-channel evidence reliability allows agents to validate consensus without surrendering independent judgment. This approach transforms simple aggregation into a process of checking for robust invariants across independent observational channels, providing a more rigorous framework for epistemic disagreement.
actions.lede: When individuals disagree, relying on group consensus requires a robust epistemic foundation rather than mere aggregation.
actions.reason: Communicating the intersection of robust analysis and group consensus models serves the judgment_and_consensus topic.
actions.title: Robustness as an Epistemic Anchor in Collective Decision-Making
